title: Gegenschein above the VLT
caption: The Gegenschein above the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A faint band of light runs diagonally from the top left to the lower right of this night sky over Paranal, home of ESO's Very Large Telescope. It is the Gegenschein, German for counter shine, a famous and extremely hard-to-observe glow that Paranal's very dark sky reveals here in full.

The Gegenschein is a faint brightening of the night sky along the ecliptic, the Sun's path across the sky, at the point directly opposite the Sun. It is caused by interplanetary dust in the Solar System reflecting sunlight back towards us.

Yuri Beletsky took the image in October 2007 with a digital camera fitted with a 10-mm wide-angle lens on a portable equatorial mount, which follows the stars as Earth turns. The total exposure lasted about 45 minutes. Conditions were excellent and the sky almost perfectly transparent, letting him record the glow's faintest details and bring out its fine structure.

understand.summary: This is a wide-angle photograph from a digital camera on a tracking mount, with a total exposure of about 45 minutes, as stated by ESO.
understand.eye: The Gegenschein is extremely faint, and the long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, revealing structure no observer could see directly.
